title: n and 2n: Haploid vs Diploid Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
Forty six, twenty three, forty six: a skin cell, a sperm or an egg, and a baby's first cell. Aarav loves number puzzles and asks why the middle number is half. The answer is a count of chromosome sets, and plants play this number game in a stranger way than we do.

You will learn what n and 2n mean, zoom from an onion root to its root tip cells, one nucleus and its sixteen chromosomes in eight pairs, and watch mitosis, meiosis and fertilisation change the count in three animated lanes. Then the three rules (meiosis halves, fertilisation doubles, mitosis copies), the plant twist of a haploid body and a diploid body, a pause and think check, a worked chromosome count for an onion flower, the exam trap, an original NEET pattern question, a recap card and three questions to answer. This is Episode 28 of our PUC Biology series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 46, 23, 46: the number puzzle
0:29 What n and 2n mean
0:54 Zoom ladder: onion root to chromosomes
1:19 Mitosis, meiosis and fertilisation, live
1:59 The three rules of the number game
2:16 The plant twist: haploid and diploid bodies + pause and think
3:09 Worked example: count the onion flower
3:39 Exam trap: can a haploid cell do mitosis?
4:05 Practice question (NEET pattern)
4:35 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Life Cycles of Major Plant Groups. In a moss, a fern and a mango tree, which phase do we actually see?
